description: The full schema of one dataset: every column (type, role, unit, value range, what a NULL means), the exact `filters` with their valid values (the keys query_dataset and aggregate accept), how the code columns join to the lookup tables (`foreign_keys`), example queries, usage notes, limitations, and null semantics. `key_metric` names the headline figure most answers want. Per column, `key_metric_grain_contributor` marks a category the headline figure is only comparable within (pin it or group by it) and `metric_component` marks the numerator and denominator of a rate. `recommended_query` is a safe default query (headline figure, the filters to pin, required single-value choices) plus a `ranking` recipe for top or bottom N. `filter_hints` lists paired filters. `non_additive` lists columns whose rows overlap, so summing across them double counts; `value_implications` lists values that imply another column's value. `year_meaning`, when set, says what `year` labels when it is not when the figures were measured. `pooled_rates` lists rates whose figure for several rows is SUM(numerator) / SUM(denominator) (aggregate with agg='weighted_rate'), not an average of the rows' rates. `series_breaks` lists years from which figures are not comparable with earlier years (each with its `reason`; `metrics`, when present, limits it to those columns), so the step into such a year is not a trend. Each category filter carries `has_total` and `requires_single_value`. verbosity='schema' drops the prose (descriptions, usage, limitations, examples) for a much smaller payload that still has everything needed to build a query; the limitations prose in the default 'full' carries the caveats. An unknown dataset returns an error listing the available ones with a 'did you mean'.

main_topic.description: Subject area: 'education' (the default), 'census', or 'immigration'. A dataset's key starts with it.
main_topic.title: Main Topic

topic.description: Dataset name, e.g. 'act_scores' (the last part of a key from list_datasets or search_datasets). The full key, e.g. 'education/gosa/act_scores', also works and sets main_topic.
topic.title: Topic

verbosity.description: 'full' (default) or 'schema' (drops the prose; keeps columns, filters and valid values, key_metric, and recommended_query).
verbosity.title: Verbosity
